name: שברים חלקיים – מונה קבוע ושלושה גורמים לינאריים (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Express

\[ {{CT:0}}\mbox{,} \]

as a sum of partial fractions.

[[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Three different linear factors: one term for each; multiply out and match coefficients.
Step 1 — The form
The rules for partial fractions are summarized below.
Rules of partial fractions. If the degree of the numerator is at least the degree of the denominator, divide first. Then each factor of the denominator gives terms:
  • a linear factor \(ax+b\): \(\dfrac{A}{ax+b}\);
  • a repeated linear factor \((ax+b)^2\): \(\dfrac{A}{ax+b}+\dfrac{B}{(ax+b)^2}\);
  • an irreducible quadratic factor \(ax^2+bx+c\): \(\dfrac{Ax+B}{ax^2+bx+c}\).
Applying these rules, we find that:

\[ {{CT:0}}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{{CT:1}}+\frac{C}{{CT:2}}\mbox{.} \]

Step 2 — Multiplying out
Multiplying both sides through by {{CT:3}}

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:4}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:5}} + {{CT:6}} + {{CT:7}}\mbox{,}\\ {{CT:4}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:8}} + {{CT:9}} + {{CT:10}}\mbox{.} \end{array} \]

Step 3 — Matching coefficients
Matching coefficients

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:11}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle 0\mbox{,}\\ {{CT:12}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle 0\mbox{,}\\ {{CT:10}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:4}}\mbox{.} \end{array} \]

So

\[ A={{CT:13}}\mbox{.} \]

Substituting this value in the other two equations we see that

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:14}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle 0\mbox{,}\\ {{CT:15}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle 0\mbox{.} \end{array} \]

Step 4 — Solving for B and C
Rearranging

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:16}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:17}}\mbox{,}\\ {{CT:18}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:19}}\mbox{.} \end{array} \]

Multiplying the first of these two equations through by {{CT:20}} we obtain:

\[ {{CT:21}}={{CT:22}}\mbox{,} \]

and subtracting the second of the pair of equations above from this equation we can eliminate C to give an equation only in B. We find that

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle B&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:23}}\mbox{,}\\ C&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:24}}\mbox{.} \end{array} \]

Step 5 — The answer
Therefore

\[ {{CT:0}}={{CT:25}}. \]
